commits.message:
[telemetry] Isolate Prometheus collector failures (#9297)

Keep scrape and health-reporting failures inside the Prometheus
collector so telemetry cannot terminate its polling thread. Expected
endpoint connection failures emit a bounded warning without a traceback;
unexpected processing and publication failures retain tracebacks for
diagnosis.

This prevents a metrics endpoint disappearing during task shutdown from
replacing the workload's actual failure with a telemetry stack trace.

commits.message:
[post-training] Add learning-progression curriculum pass (#9294)

Add a catalog-level learning graph that implements the proposal's
epsilon condition: mastery of A should materially
improve the chance of some success on a recurring family of entry-level
B tasks. Capability generation continues to
leave embedded prerequisite arrays empty. The published v3 catalog
clears the 17 legacy hard-dependency entries and
stores the reviewed graph once at the catalog root.

The production pass is subject-local. Each of the 45 subjects receives
one compact packet, one Sol/high proposer,
and one independent Sol/high reviewer. Agents do not receive the full
catalog, and the workflow does not run
per-capability, per-edge, or semantic repair calls. Every edge records
an enabled scope, artifact-substitution test,
transfer basis, and two concise task-family witnesses. Cross-subject
progression remains a follow-up rather than
being inferred from partial context.

The final graph contains 1,812 acyclic edges. Proposers emitted 1,631;
reviewers accepted 1,596, rejected 35, and
supplied 216 complete omissions. Subject graphs contain 19–78 edges and
reach a maximum learning stage of eight. D15
required one mechanical retry after its first combined result contained
a cycle. Total measured usage was 4.85M
tokens, compared with 16.28M for the original catalog build and 8.92M
for the production repair wave.

The canonical artifact is

`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/task-curriculum/catalogs/2026.09.20-subject-local-v3-0ce32038771d/curriculum.json`
(SHA-256
`0ce32038771d4fb0c66498f29604474d6766040e8917f894b31940a6a828149a`). The
deterministic evidence archive
SHA-256 is
`84a1ba4284360ba3e722be7f06206588296dc3c25027300415002c9f187d779a`. The
one-off human viewer is
https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/67f69132-2ef4-4c9e-b8b5-77cabd126442/
(revision 9); it exposes hierarchy and
within-subject learning-stage views, edge evidence, and a separate
capability-scores tab.


Follow-up to #9232. Part of #9193.

[post-training] Publish cross-domain task curriculum (#9232)

Publish the 45-subject cross-domain v2 curriculum as an immutable typed
JSON artifact. The 3.6 MB payload stays in external storage. The catalog
contains 2,405 nodes: 1,999 assignable capabilities and 406
organizational groups. Runtime consumers validate it directly with
Pydantic. The 45-subject inventory is a separate typed S3 artifact;
prior YAML catalogs remain immutable rollback artifacts.

The production pass attempted one bounded repair on 42 subjects and
retained three accepted v3 graphs. Anonymous same-call review selected
41 repairs and tied D32, whose baseline was preserved. Mean holistic
score rose from 78.36 to 92.81. Twenty-four subjects are `pilot_ready`;
21 remain explicitly provisional after the one-repair stopping rule. The
1,001/1,080 frozen fit is a reused diagnostic because the older baseline
had seen an earlier fit summary.

A final routing audit placed all 24 practical TaskTrove shell,
repository-workspace, and bug-repair tasks in D02. Twenty-one had one
complete capability home. The three misses cover unrelated operations
and do not justify another catch-all. Evaluation-policy and AAII
metadata found subject homes across all 45 roots; ten benchmark entries
measure cross-domain task mechanics instead of subject knowledge.

The canonical catalog is
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/task-curriculum/catalogs/2026.09.19-json-1faada4eeda8/publish/curriculum.json`,
SHA-256
`1faada4eeda8368a7834602e88f8f3fb97e35a4baf5dedc2bae10a5dffbfc58b`. The
same immutable prefix contains the summary, anonymous comparison,
routing audit, evidence archive, and manifest. Marina viewer revision 6
serves the pinned JSON at
https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/67f69132-2ef4-4c9e-b8b5-77cabd126442/v/6/.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[grafana] Share bounded Finelog datasets across panels (#9286)

Move repeated Finelog panel SQL for Node Details, Zephyr, Training,
Runs, RL, Accelerators, Jobs, and Home behind fixed Grafana bridge
endpoints. Panels with the same identity and time window share one
cached dataset; concurrent cold requests coalesce, and each panel
selects a named local projection. Cold dataset builds use one source for
Node and Zephyr, three for Training, two for Runs, three for RL and
Accelerators, and five for Jobs. Selector queries remain separate.

The shared runner centralizes identity and window validation, SQL
rendering, source and projection budgets, cache keys, and serialized
DuckDB projection. DuckDB uses one thread, a 512 MB memory limit, and no
disk spill. Domain limits cap identities, source rows or samples,
projected rows, time windows, and point counts; the bridge-wide row
limit remains an upper bound. Requests that exceed a budget return HTTP
400 and ask the operator to narrow the request.

The consolidated sources preserve panel-specific semantics: GPU power is
averaged per device before fleet sums, run ownership is ranked before
selected-run filtering, active-run freshness uses training metrics, top
resource rankings remain independent and cluster-scoped, stale devices
remain visible, and RL percentiles are computed once at the panel bucket
grain.

## Live Finelog comparison

A sequential replay against the hub used one Training run over the fixed
2026-09-19 16:30–19:30 UTC window:

- `origin/main`: 16 successful panel queries, 16.88 seconds of summed
query time, 1,232 rows, and 62 KB of panel responses.
- This branch: three successful source queries, 3.21 seconds of summed
query time, then 0.25 seconds of local projection. The sources returned
2,275 rows and 608 KB, and projected 1,232 rows.

This comparison covers one Training run and sequential execution. It
demonstrates lower query count and summed query time for that replay,
not end-to-end Grafana page latency, concurrent p95 behavior, or lower
transfer volume.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[grafana] Make vLLM runs easier to triage (#9274)

Both inference pages put run triage above the charts. Query health
distinguishes available detail, summary-only data, empty telemetry,
timeouts, and sample-limit rejection. Run attention shows a
selected-range count gap when first-token observations exceed
`request_success_total` finishes, then points to the evaluator in Iris.
A partial or active window can produce the same gap, and separate vLLM
failure and timeout counters are excluded. The cue does not classify
failed requests. The diagnostics page links the selected or manually
entered serve to Iris and gives general guidance for checking its
evaluator.

For the [64K AIME24
serve](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fheld%2Feval-20260916-212517-grug-aime-pareto-today-20260916-d7d3%2Finference-aa956e649f044c9ba12a0de164895732?cluster=marin),
the first seven hours show 156 coherent first-token observations and 16
recorded `request_success_total` finishes; the full selection shows 160
and 16. Generated-token totals are 6,013,445 and 6,203,035,
respectively, and all 29 hourly bins match independent raw counter
calculations. The linked
[evaluator](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fheld%2Feval-20260916-212517-grug-aime-pareto-today-20260916-d7d3%2Feval-aime24-64k-ac462950?cluster=marin)
logged repeated proxy 504s after 2100 seconds, retries, and 15 terminal
request failures. Those are client and proxy observations; the server
count gap does not establish their cause.

Select up to seven hours for engine, latency, and outcome detail. Longer
ranges use a bounded reset-aware summary with hourly generated tokens,
observed waiting and KV-cache peaks, and native inter-token latency. The
picker scans only the first seven hours of a longer selection; an exact
serve ID can be entered when it omits a later session. The detail source
scan matches current main's merged #8930 query apart from whitespace. On
the 64K window, its live fetch returned 1,030 compact series rows (11.28
MB) in 2.77 seconds. The full-run summary fetched 104 series rows (4.38
MB) in 3.87 seconds and projected them locally in 0.42 seconds. One
panel-data source fetch is shared by all 31 targets across the two pages
per selected range. The identity picker is a separate bounded query.
These measurements do not establish a speedup over current main.

The full-run summary omits latency tails, output-length distribution,
per-engine detail, and client or proxy time. Historical scalar
histograms work here; bundled histogram support remains in Ahmed's
pending #9276 and MarinSkyRL #694. The dashboards have not been
deployed, so final Grafana rendering is unverified.

Part of #8929.
